steps.title: Ripe and spicy
steps.body: Grenache gives medium to full-bodied reds with strawberry, raspberry, red cherry, white pepper, dried herbs and, with age, leather and toffee. Colour is often paler than expected. Tannins are soft to medium, acidity low to medium, and alcohol high, often 14.5 to 16%.

steps.title: Spanish origins
steps.body: Grenache, Garnacha in Spain, probably comes from Aragón, in north-east Spain; some argue for Sardinia, where it's called Cannonau. It loves heat and drought, and accumulates sugar fast, which explains its high alcohol. Thin skins mean paler colour and softer tannin. It oxidises easily, so it browns early.

steps.prompt: Why is Grenache often high in alcohol?
options: It accumulates sugar quickly in heat
steps.explanation: Grenache ripens to high sugar levels, which become alcohol.

steps.title: Spotting it
steps.body: Look for medium ruby colour, often with an orange rim early, ripe red fruit, white pepper and herbs, a warm, high-alcohol feel and soft tannins. Compared with Syrah, it's paler and redder-fruited; compared with Pinot Noir, warmer and riper.

steps.prompt: Grenache usually gives deeply coloured, tannic wines.
steps.explanation: Not true. Its thin skins give paler colour and softer tannin.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Grenache gives strawberry, spice and high alcohol
It comes from Spain and loves heat and drought
Thin skins mean paler colour and soft tannin
